outcome.technical: R3: guard-release.py gains tree_verdict(why, tree, project, session_id, now) returning (VERDICT_CLEAR|VERDICT_RELEASED|VERDICT_REFUSED, text) plus _released_over(); decide() now only routes trees through it; release.py release_verdict() is two lines calling gr.tree_verdict with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, so its own restated control flow and the 'could not read the release status' branch are gone. Consequence worth the reviewer's eye: an unreadable plan now follows the guard's own rule (refused with the guard's UNKNOWN sentence without a slot, released over with an armed slot, as the guard's gr18 and gr14 already did), where release.py used to refuse an unreadable plan even with an armed slot. R1: verify.sh gains run_noted (runs run, then prints the step log indented six spaces, as show_failure does, only when quiet, not --list, and the step passed; run sets STEP_PASSED); the release slice's 'the plan carries no open bug or held phase' row uses it. R2: release.py cases rl21 (unparsable and missing plan refused, both lists named UNKNOWN) and rl21b (armed slot releases over it, second direction). Further cases: rl22 (release_verdict names tree_verdict and none of read_bugs/read_held_phases/bypass_armed/refusal, AST), rl23 and rl23b (verify.sh functions cut out and run under sh over an open-bug plan with an armed slot: the passing step prints BUG-4 and the keyword once beneath its ok row; under --list it prints the label and no verdict), guard gr72..gr72e (decide and tree_verdict agree across open bug/no slot, armed, clean, unreadable/no slot, unreadable/armed) and gr73 (decide calls tree_verdict and not the readers). Mutations in a throwaway tree of copies (tools/, .claude/hooks) with the rest symlinked, anchors asserted to match once; baseline 65/65 and 109/109, then: M1 run_noted prints nothing -> rl23 red (64/65); M2 unreadable list read as nothing -> rl21 and rl21b red for both plan shapes (61/65), gr72d, gr72e red (103/109); M3 slot ignored -> rl21b x2, rl23, rl20b red (57/65), gr72b, gr72e red (104/109); M4 release_verdict re-reads the slot -> rl22 red (64/65); M5 decide re-reads the slot -> gr73 red (108/109); M6 verdict never refuses -> rl21 x2 red among 17 (48/65), gr72, gr72d red among 30 (79/109). The throwaway tree was removed. Gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/release.py .claude/hooks/guard-release.py tools/gate-parity.py tests/test__deps.py, run unpiped, exit 0, 4/4 files ok (guard-release 109 cases, test__deps 254, gate-parity 93, release 65). sh -n tools/verify.sh exit 0. I did not run release.py run or verify.sh --release. Dependants: verify.sh (other steps and run itself behave as before; only a new function, one flag variable and one call site changed; ci.yml, affected.py, gate-parity read --list output which is unchanged because run_noted calls run) still correct. release.py (release_verdict keeps its signature and (allowed, text) return, so cmd_permitted, release_permitted and tests/test_audit_task.py are untouched; only the unreadable-plan wording changed and nothing else greps the old sentence) still correct. guard-release.py (decide keeps its signature and None-or-reason return; arm-release-bypass.py, settings.json and the lints use the existing functions, none removed) still correct.
outcome.descriptive: The release check now prints what an armed bypass releases over even when it passes, an unreadable plan is covered by cases, and the hook and release.py take one shared decision function instead of two copies.
